conventions.convention: The oscillator has real parameters m>0, c≥0, k∈ℝ and continuous forcing on a time interval with nonempty interior. Solutions are twice differentiable; included endpoints use domain-relative derivatives. Physical meanings and units are supplied by physical consumers.

Convolution integrals are oriented. The C¹ matrix kernel is defined on an open interval containing every difference of two points of the forcing interval; the convolution lemma states differentiation at interior times.

Periodic averaging uses continuous f:ℝ×O→ℝⁿ with continuous state partial derivatives, period P>0, average P⁻¹∫₀ᴾf(s,x)ds, and deviation g(t,x)=∫₀ᵗ(f(s,x)−f̄(x))ds, extended periodically with g(0,x)=0.

The action-angle datum has C² functions on open extension domains, radian angle period 2π, K=h+εk, frequency ω=∂Ih, and branch equations I′=−ε∂θk, θ′=∂Ih+ε∂Ik, s′=ε. The drift generator is g=(k−⟨k⟩)/ω wherever ω≠0.

Finite-time linearization uses the Euclidean state norm and its induced operator norm, a strictly positive initial norm δ, a closed ball contained in the open field domain, and the strict smallness condition δe^(LT)<r.
Averaging assumes the averaged trajectory stays in the closed ball of radius R−ρ throughout [0,A/ε], with 0<ρ<R and εK<ρ. Its conclusion concerns that horizon only.

Adiabatic drift assumes an existing branch solution trapped in the stated compact action and parameter intervals and |∂Ih|≥ω₀>0 there. Trapping and existence of an applicable chart are hypotheses, not conclusions.
The sinusoidal response permits Ω=0 and f₀=0; resonance requires c=0 and Ω=√(k/m), and unboundedness additionally requires f₀≠0. The amplitude-maximum proposition assumes c>0 and f₀≠0.

load_bearing.statement: For m>0, c≥0, k∈ℝ and continuous f:I→ℝ, the oscillator equation is mx″+cx′+kx=f(t), equivalent to the phase system (x,v)′=(v,(f(t)−cv−kx)/m), on the specified nondegenerate intervals.

For n≥1, A∈Mₙ(ℝ), t₀∈ℝ, z₀∈ℝⁿ and continuous b:ℝ→ℝⁿ, E(t)=Σₖ₌₀∞tᵏAᵏ/k! is C¹, E′=AE=EA, E(u+v)=E(u)E(v), and ‖E(u)‖≤e^(‖A‖|u|). The curve z(t)=E(t−t₀)z₀+∫ₜ₀ᵗE(t−s)b(s)ds solves z′=Az+b globally; every interval solution through the same datum is its restriction.

For m>0, c≥0 and k>0, all interval solutions of mx″+cx′+kx=0 are exactly the two-exponential family when Δ>0, the family (A+Bt)e^(−ct/(2m)) when Δ=0, and e^(−γt)(A cos(ωt)+B sin(ωt)) when Δ<0. Every datum at zero determines exactly one global member, and every local solution uniquely extends to one.

For m>0, c≥0 and k≤0, all homogeneous interval solutions are affine when k=c=0, A+Be^(−ct/m) when k=0<c, and Ae^(λ₊t)+Be^(λ₋t) when k<0, where λ₋<0<λ₊. Local solutions uniquely extend globally; in the repulsive case e^(λ₊t) is an explicit unbounded solution.

For n≥1, nondegenerate interval I, t₀∈I, open U⊇I−I, a C¹ matrix kernel g:U→Mₙ(ℝ), and continuous f:I→ℝⁿ, F(t)=∫ₜ₀ᵗg(t−s)f(s)ds is differentiable at every interior t, with F′(t)=g(0)f(t)+∫ₜ₀ᵗg′(t−s)f(s)ds; F is C¹ on the interior.

For m>0, c≥0, k≥0, continuous f on a nondegenerate interval I and prescribed displacement and velocity at t₀∈I, there is exactly one solution on I, including domain-relative derivatives at included endpoints. It is x(t)=x_h(t)+∫ₜ₀ᵗg(t−s)f(s)ds, where g is the global homogeneous solution with g(0)=0 and g′(0)=1/m.

For continuous state-locally-Lipschitz F:U→ℝⁿ on open U∋0, assume the closed radius-r ball lies in U and ‖F(z)−Az‖≤C‖z‖², ‖F(z)‖≤L‖z‖ there. For δ=‖z₀‖>0 and T>0 with δe^(LT)<r, the maximal nonlinear solution exists on [0,T], satisfies ‖z(t)‖≤δe^(Lt), and differs from y′=Ay, y(0)=z₀ by at most Cδ²∫₀ᵗe^(‖A‖(t−s))e^(2Ls)ds≤Cδ²te^((‖A‖+2L)t).

For the periodic averaging datum and a closed state ball with ‖f‖≤M and state-Lipschitz constant L, the average has the same bounds; the periodic deviation satisfies ‖g‖≤2MP, has state-Lipschitz constant 2LP, satisfies ∂tg=f−f̄, has continuous first partial derivatives, and ‖Dₓg‖≤2LP on that ball.

For the periodic datum with ‖f‖≤M and ‖Dₓf‖≤L on the closed radius-R state ball, set B=2MP, B₁=2LP and K=e^(LA)[B+(LB+B₁M)A]. If ε,A>0, 0<ρ<R, the averaged solution through x₀ stays in the radius-(R−ρ) ball on [0,A/ε], and εK<ρ, then the exact solution through x₀ exists on that whole interval and ‖x(t)−y(t)‖≤εK there.

For the C² periodic branch datum, ε,A,ω₀>0, compact intervals K⊆J and S₀⊆S with |∂Ih|≥ω₀ on K×S₀, and a branch solution on [0,A/ε] with s(0)=s₀∈S₀ trapped in K×S₀, |I(t)−I(0)|≤ε[2 sup|g|+A sup|∂Ig∂θk−∂θg∂Ik−∂sg|], with both suprema over K×[0,2π]×S₀ and g=(k−⟨k⟩)/∂Ih.

concerns.concern: Fact L2 asserts that 'compositions of continuous functions are continuous' and cites thm-composition-with-a-continuous-function. That supplier proves Riemann integrability of a continuous outer function composed with an integrable inner function; it does not prove continuity of composition. Step 1.1 uses L2 to establish continuity of √|x|. The conclusion is correct and the missing continuity argument is elementary, but the named composition supplier does not establish the cited proposition.

Verification step 1.1 says 'The curve z(t)=(1−t,−1) ... lies in ℝ×U there'. The curve value is in ℝ² and belongs to U; its time-state graph (t,z(t)) belongs to ℝ×U⊆ℝ³. The stated membership mixes the curve with its graph. This is a wording/type slip; the domain and maximality conclusions remain supported.

alerts.finding: Fact F5, headed 'Scalar oscillator calculus', cites thm-cm-homogeneous-oscillator-solution-classification and says the scalar equations have 'the affine family for λ_i=0'. The cited classification explicitly assumes k>0, so it cannot supply λ_i=0. The zero-stiffness family is supplied by prop-cm-oscillator-degenerate-and-repulsive-cases, or by the correctly stated free-mode theory already cited in F2. Step 2.2 cites both F2 and F5, so the motion conclusion has support, but F5's attribution extends its named mathematical supplier outside its hypotheses.

seams_checked.note: Cylinder-local uniqueness is propagated along connected solution intervals. Forced modal response uses the quadratic-mode supplier's algebraic diagonalization, explicitly distinguishes its zero-containing interval convention, and verifies responses at arbitrary t₀.
Linearization and averaging apply compact continuation only after trapping their time-state graphs in compact subsets of the actual open ODE domains.
The adiabatic example bounds action, angle and slow parameter near any proposed finite endpoint before invoking autonomous compact continuation.

The adiabatic example verifies local state Lipschitz continuity; the nonuniqueness example explicitly fails that condition. The domain-escape example uses maximal solutions on its restricted state domain.
No direct approximation-result invocation was found in this A page's listed item bodies. Its declared prerequisite is not used to assert an additional oscillator or approximation conclusion.
The drag-terminal-velocity example applies forced scalar solvability with k=0 and constant forcing, and uses the c>0 degenerate homogeneous family with the correct initial coefficients.

Oscillator model identification, shifted homogeneous classifications, strictly damped decay, sinusoidal response and amplitude maxima retain the relevant parameter conditions. The positive-frequency physical drive convention narrows the mathematical supplier.
Damping regimes and driven-response checks specialize the correct classified families. The bounded-drive counterexample uses nonzero undamped resonant forcing, as required for unboundedness.

Positive, zero and negative modes use their appropriate scalar suppliers. Forced modal response retains nonnegative stiffness. Linearization translates the equilibrium and normalizes coordinates; weak-damping averaging retains the state bounds, horizon, smallness and averaged-trajectory trapping.

The triatomic example's F5 attributes the affine λ_i=0 family to the homogeneous classification restricted to k>0. This specific citation mismatch is routed in alerts; F2 independently supplies the zero-mode conclusion. Other inspected scalar classifications respect their parameter ranges.

Adiabatic invariance uses a fixed canonical radian chart, C² open extensions, the exact branch equations, nonvanishing frequency and compact trapping. Its corrected-action identity and drift estimate match the mathematical supplier.
The finite-time clause translates an equilibrium to zero, explicitly requires δ>0, verifies the remainder and growth hypotheses, and retains δe^(LT)<r and the finite horizon.

Boundary-value nonuniqueness uses the undamped positive-stiffness classification; the two-mass proposition separates positive and zero stiffness. The pendulum proposition restates the linearization hypotheses and finite-time conclusion faithfully.
Two-mass checks distinguish oscillatory and affine modes. The pendulum check specializes the finite-time estimate with the stated remainder constant, operator norm and smallness condition.
